description:
Problem: judge() counts a finding only when its path string exactly equals a changed path (_project/scripts/oracle_reviewers/protocol.py:492, item.file in scope). A finding cited with a different Unicode form (NFD for an NFC path), a case variant, or a symlink alias of a changed file is treated as out of scope and not counted, so a real defect can turn into SHIP. Reproduced in the 2026-10-26 review (benchbox/Café.py cited in NFD). #3419's title claimed canonical comparison but only fixed escaping.

Outcome: finding paths are compared to changed paths after Unicode NFC normalisation and symlink-alias resolution inside the head tree; a case-only variant that matches exactly one changed path counts as that path; an ambiguous match counts against the decision (never silently dropped). Findings on genuinely unchanged files stay out of scope as today.

Decision gates:
1. Reproduce the NFD case as a failing test on develop before the fix.
2. Canonicalisation may only move findings into scope, never out of it; prove with tests.
